newsitem.title: USA: IBM deal offers wide choice -- U.S. bankers.
newsitem.headline: IBM deal offers wide choice -- U.S. bankers.

text.p: U.S. bankers participating in a technological venture with International Business Machine Corp. called Integrion Financial Networks said the alliance will offer their customers a broad choice of services.
James Dixon, Chief Information Officer at Charlotte, North Carolina-based NationsBank Corp. said "the broadest possible choice" is being offered "to the end user consumer."
Dixon spoke at a news conference attended by chief executives of Barnett Banks Inc., Bank One Corp., KeyCorp, Royal Bank of Canada, as well as Louis Gerstner, Chairman and Chief Executive of IBM.
A total of 15 banks are participating in the Integrion venture. Pilot projects on Integrion will be started by Bank One and Nations Bank in early 1997.
The Integrion network will be open to all banks in North America, participants in the news conference said.
Questioned about the relatively slow start so far of banking at home via personal computer, Charles Rice, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Barnett Banks, said "The demand is there."

Gerstner of IBM said electronic commerce, in which consumers buy goods and services via computer, could grow to $600 billion a year within 10 years. He said by contrast electronic commerce was now only running at about $700 million a year.
Several of the bankers participating in the news conference said the partnership with IBM will lower the cost of developing technology for the banks.
Gerstner said IBM would provide service to Integrion. "We are an enabler and a partner, not a competitor, to the banks," he said.
